answer: One concrete defence is a bonded, hardware-anchored identity. Each agent posts a stake locked for several epochs and unlockable only by a proof derived from a unique device attestation. A sybil farm therefore pays a full bond plus a fresh attestation per key, so its marginal cost equals an honest member's. Attestation strings are kept as cipher commitments in append-only strata, like shale layers, letting the protocol flag two identities sharing a root and slash both bonds. Honest agents recover stake plus uptime yield; attackers forfeit capital.
